subject: Engine trio shortlist & decision ladder for Clara pilot
messages:

Subject: Thanks — quick follow-up and questions from today's demo

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — found the latency graphs and live token billing really helpful. A couple of quick follow-ups so our engineering team can scope a pilot:  

- Primary workloads: document Q&A (short user queries, average response ~120 tokens) and automated discharge summaries (longer outputs, average ~600 tokens).
- Latency target: we want median tail ~<250ms for interactive Q&A and <600ms 95th for summaries.
- Cost sensitivity: ideally under $6k/mo for the pilot (targeting ~150k user queries/month).
- Security: we need confirmation of tenant isolation and audit logs for the pilot.

Could you send a short recommended engine shortlist (3 variants) with a concise rationale (cost/latency/quality tradeoffs), sample prompt packs we can test, and links to the benchmark artifacts you referenced? Also please include any redlines or regression-guardrail recommendations for the rollout (canary %, automatic fallback behavior).

I've attached the call recording and our initial requirements PDF for reference.

Thanks — Kate

Clara Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Su <kate.su@clarahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-04-14T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks — quick follow-up and questions from today's demo

Hi Kate — great to chat. Below is a concise "decision ladder" (engine trio) that balances cost, latency, and quality for the two Clara use-cases. I prioritized options you can pilot quickly with predictable fallbacks.

1) rt-cost-compact (4-bit int quantized) — recommended pilot default for high-volume Q&A
   - Expected latency (512-token window): median 80–130ms, p95 ~220ms (on our dedicated GPU pool).
   - Quality: high for retrieval-augmented Q&A; slightly lower on long-form summarization (risk of compression artifacts).
   - Cost: ~ $1.8k/mo at your target QPS (est. ~150k queries/month at avg 120 tokens).
   - When to use: production Q&A path where cost/latency balance matters.

2) rt-balanced-16 (fp16 weights, medium context) — general-purpose balanced option
   - Expected latency: median 120–200ms, p95 ~350ms.
   - Quality: solid for both Q&A and summaries; better long-form coherence than compact.
   - Cost: ~ $3.9k/mo for pilot volume.
   - When to use: mixed traffic or where slightly higher quality is needed; good default for canary.

3) rt-high-qual (fp32 / larger context) — for the heaviest, highest-accuracy summary path
   - Expected latency: median 250–420ms, p95 up to ~800ms for long sequences.
   - Quality: top-tier: best factuality and coherence on discharge summaries.
   - Cost: ~ $9.5k/mo if majority of traffic runs here (we recommend limited scope).
   - When to use: finalization and human-in-the-loop review flows; small percentage of traffic.

Tradeoffs summary: lower-precision variants give strong cost wins and better latency but carry higher regression risk on subtle summarization fidelity. The decision ladder is: default to rt-cost-compact for Q&A; route summaries to rt-balanced-16; escalate to rt-high-qual for edge cases or review flows.

Artifacts I attached: benchmark_summary.csv (token-latency/cost matrix, dataset: med-qna + discharge-summaries-small), prompt_pack_v1.md (seed prompts & perturbations). Live links below.

Quick asks to size the pilot properly: average tokens per request for each workload, peak QPS (estimate), and any compliance controls (e.g., must-run-only-in-vpc). With that I'll draft a recommended canary rollout (percentages + regression checks).

Links: https://drive.redwood.ai/clh/benchmarks/CLH-4091-v1

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: benchmark_summary.csv, prompt_pack_v1.md

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2029-04-15T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: recommended engine trio — ops notes and regression guardrails

Hi Kate — adding a few operations-focused notes so the pilot avoids common pitfalls:  

- Rollout plan: 5% canary on rt-balanced-16 for 72 hours with synthetic prompt perturbation suite (included in prompt_pack_v1.md) and automatic daily regression report. If no regressions -> 25% for 48h -> 50% then steady-state.
- Auto-fallback: configure routing rules so that when p95 latency >650ms or error-rate >1% the request routes to rt-cost-compact (QPS permitting). We recommend an adaptive fallback window (3 consecutive 1-min checks) to prevent oscillation.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for the Q&A path (saves ~30% token compute at the same latency).
- Batching: for summary pipelines we recommend small, latency-aware batching windows (20–50ms) to improve throughput without degrading p95 substantially.
- Regression guardrails: compare a saved baseline on ROUGE / factuality spike metrics + hallucination rate using the perturbation set. If regression detected, automatically divert 100% of affected prompt templates to rt-high-qual while we investigate.

I'll attach an ops-checklist with tests, traces to collect (token-level latency, kv-cache hit rate, generation entropy), and suggested runbook entries.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Product Manager, Runtime & Ops — Redwood Inference

Attachments: ops-checklist.md

- rt-cost-compact (if 70% of traffic): ~ $1,800/mo
- rt-balanced-16 (if 25% of traffic): ~ $3,900/mo
- rt-high-qual (if 5% of traffic): ~ $1,200/mo
Estimated total: ~ $6,900/mo (within your stated target range; we can tune routing to bring this closer to $6k).

Procurement steps: 1) Pilot SOW + security addendum (I attached the SOW draft), 2) NDA / standard DPA (we received your signed NDA), 3) pilot kick-off & invoice. If you want reserved capacity instead of hosted, we can provide an alternate pricing sheet.
